text:
incident-bot: ALERT: streaming-decode p99 spike detected for model:redwood/gpt-large (us-west-2) — p95 420ms -> 1.2s, p99 1.6s -> 6.8s, error-rate 0.8% (decodes timing out). pagefault/swap indications on 8 nodes. Paging alarm: pager #INC-9342 triggered.

jenna w.: paging pager received. I'm on it. tagging eng-runtime + ops-sre. @liam can you dump quick p95/p99 histograms and which pools are affected?

liam k.: grabbing metrics — looks concentrated on streaming endpoints for sequence-length >1024 and for model variants using FlashAttention kernels (gpu-pool: rt-prod-1a, rt-prod-1b). p95 graph: https://metrics.redwood.internal/streams/p95?from=now-30m (shortlink). sample tail traces: 
```
trace_id=0x7f9a; decode_ms=6820; model=gpt-large; kernel=trt8-flashattn; node=rt-prod-1a-03
trace_id=0x7fb2; decode_ms=6120; oom=false; pagefaults=high; nvml_gpu_util=95%
```
Most of these started ~00:12 UTC after a background kernel/compilepath rollout that completed ~00:05.

miguel (eng-runtime): I saw the rollout. We pushed a new compilepath and a TRT8+FlashAttention tune that enabled an aggressive kernel fusion flag (\`--enable-fast-flash\`) across those pools last night. That flag improved latency for 99% of inferences under normal lengths, but can increase working set/KV pressure for long sequences -> more GPU memory churn and pagefaults on certain GPU drivers.

ops-sre: Confirming dmesg on rt-prod-1a-03 shows repeated page faultbacks around 00:12: 
```
[00:12:10] nvidia: GPU pagefault: ctx 0x2c -> remap triggered
[00:12:11] nvlink: tdr: evicting KV cache entry seq=98765
[00:12:12] nvidia: process decode: pagefault stall 4500ms
```
We also see elevated kernel preemption counts and several kernel module warnings tied to the new compilepath.

jenna w.: customer-impact? maya? any support tickets? Should we open a status page?

maya (prod-support): Two customers (acct-8241, acct-935) reported degraded streaming in us-west-2 since ~00:15 UTC, both have active sessions hitting long sequences. We're drafting a PSAT notice once we confirm mitigation. CSMs notified.

liam k.: quick mitigation options (ranked):
1) Roll back the compilepath/flag on affected pools (fastest if we have rollback image).
2) Route long-sequence requests to fallback model variant (smaller KV footprint / quantized) via runtime routing policy.
3) Scale up nodes pinned to older kernel and shift traffic away from flagged nodes.
4) Toggle KV-cache eviction thresholds (but that's risky w.r.t correctness).

miguel (eng-runtime): I can do #2 + #3 now. We don't have a safe canary rollback image for the compilepath on every node without a short rebuild (image creation takes ~15min).

ops-sre: I'm standing by for the routing change. If we can reroute long sequences to fallback model we'll see immediate P99 improvement for those sessions.

jenna w.: Proceed with routing fallback + scale pinned nodes. Do it in small steps and watch errors. post commands and I'll monitor.

miguel (eng-runtime): running patch now. Command to add routing rule for sequences >1024:
```
curl -X POST https://runtime-api.internal/routing/policies \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $RUNTIME_TOKEN' \
  -d '{"name":"fallback-long-seq-usw2","predicate":{"seq_len_gt":1024,"region":"us-west-2"},"route_to":"gpt-large-quantized-v1","priority":50}'
```
Applying... response: 202 Accepted.

ops-sre: also applying k8s scale for pinned-nodes: 
```
kubectl -n runtime scale deployment rt-pinned-oldkernel --replicas=4
```
Scaling up.. pods coming up (rt-pinned-oldkernel-2 -> ready).

liam k.: after routing rule + scale (5m): p95 now 380ms, p99 740ms for the affected traffic slice. Overall p99 across cluster dropped from 6.8s -> 1.1s. Error-rate down to 0.12%. Nice.

maya (prod-support): Customer tickets updated. Status page draft: "Partial degradation for streaming in US-WEST-2 affecting large-sequence sessions; mitigation in progress; routing fallback applied." Recommend posting in 10m if stable.

jenna w.: good progress. Next steps: short-term -> keep routing fallback + scale until we can do a safe compilepath rollback or rebuild. Medium-term -> reproduce locally and build a compile without --enable-fast-flash to verify working set impact. Long-term -> improve canary gating for memory-pressure regressions.

miguel (eng-runtime): I'll trigger a staged rollback plan for flagged pools. If rollback images exist, we can roll per-pool; if not, I'll open a rebuild PR for compilepath without that flag and request expedited CI (estimate 30-45m).

ops-sre: I'll keep an eye on node telemetry and remove nodes from rotation if pagefaults reappear. Also will collect full nvml traces for the hot nodes and upload: s3://redwood-eng/infra/rt-prod-1a-03/nvml-traces/6743211123.tar.gz

liam k.: quick forensic snippet — stack trace of decode kernel during stall:
```
#0  nv_run_kernel+0x12b
#1  tvm_run_op+0x4d
#2  flash_attn_dispatch+0x90
#3  decode_step+0x1e3
```
This points at FlashAttention dispatch path interacting with new fused kernel.

jenna w.: prepare handoff for next oncall in 30m. Summarize what we did and what is outstanding.

oncall-next: I'll take next shift. Handoff notes:
- Incident root: aggressive compilepath flag (--enable-fast-flash) increased GPU working set for long sequences causing pagefaults and decode tail spikes.
- Actions performed: routing fallback to gpt-large-quantized-v1 for seq>1024 in us-west-2, scaled pinned nodes to older-kernel pool, collected nvml traces, notified CSMs, drafted status page.
- Metrics now: p95 380ms, p99 740ms for affected traffic; error-rate back to baseline.
- Outstanding: roll back compilepath across affected pools OR rebuild compile without flag; reproduce in staging; create PR for canary gating on memory pressure; post status page if stable for 10m.
- Links: runbook: https://runbook.redwood/internal/paging-decode, traces: https://traces.redwood/internal/trace/6743211123, nvml s3 link above.

jenna w.: added followups: ACTION-1129 (rebuild compilepath without flag), ACTION-1130 (improve canary tests), ACTION-1131 (postmortem draft). Assigning to miguel and liam.

miguel (eng-runtime): opened PR: https://git.internal/redwood/compilepath/pulls/498 (wip, removing --enable-fast-flash flag, CI running). ETA for merge + image: ~40min.

liam k.: verifying logs for the last 10m, no new pagefault flares. Recommend we update customers now.

maya (prod-support): publishing status: https://status.redwood.com/incidents/9342 — note: recovery in progress; mitigation applied; will update when compilepath rollback completed.

jenna w.: handing off. Oncall-next will monitor 30m then close if stable. Great coordination — :tada:

oncall-next: acknowledged. I'll monitor for 60m and escalate if p99 creeps above 1s again.

incident-bot: Incident resolved (mitigated) at 6743212350; postmortem required if full rollback required.
